examples.en: The teacher designates the pages to read for homework.
The company assigned me a specific seat.
Where will you set the meeting place?
Thank you for assigning me a seat.
I pick the recipient and send the email.
It is a place the mayor designated as the new park.

explain: '정하다'보다 딱딱해서 안내문, 서류, 규칙에 자주 나와요. 여러 가운데 하나를 콕 집어 말할 때 쓰고, '지정 좌석', '지정석'처럼 명사 앞에도 붙어요.
explain_en: It sounds more formal than '정하다' and often appears in notices, documents and rules. You use it when you pick one thing out of several, and it also attaches to nouns, as in '지정 좌석' and '지정석'.

examples.en: Mom pan-fries kimchi in a frying pan.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 부침개를 지져 먹어요.
examples.en: On rainy days we fry pancakes and eat them.
I pan-fried the bindaetteok in oil.
I pan-fry the tofu until golden and add the sauce.

examples.ko: 양념을 넣고 자작하게 지진 두부가 맛있어요.
examples.en: Tofu braised with seasoning and just a little broth is tasty.
What will you cook in the pan tonight?

explain: 기름을 조금 두르고 부치거나, 국물을 적게 해서 졸이듯 익히는 요리에 써요. 국물이 많은 요리는 '끓이다'라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: It is used for frying in a little oil or simmering a dish down until little broth remains. Dishes with a lot of broth use '끓이다' instead.

examples.en: The police investigate the cause of the accident.
This case is being investigated now.
It is a matter the prosecutors have investigated since yesterday.
They widened the investigation to find the culprit.

examples.ko: 내일부터 경찰이 이 일을 수사할 거예요.
examples.en: The police will start investigating this from tomorrow.

examples.ko: 경찰이 수사해서 밝힌 내용을 뉴스에서 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw on the news what the police revealed after investigating.

explain: 경찰이나 검찰이 범죄를 조사할 때 써요. 학교나 회사에서 일의 이유를 알아보는 것은 '조사하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when the police or prosecutors look into a crime. When a school or company looks into the reason for something, you say '조사하다'.

examples.en: The children are playing around in the yard.
You must not mess around during class.
My little brother played around with the puppy.
I broke a cup while horsing around with a friend.
The way they play around is so cute.

examples.ko: 저는 지금 진지해요. 장난할 기분이 아니에요.
examples.en: I am serious now. I am not in the mood to joke around.

explain: 보통 '장난치다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '장난하다'는 아이가 놀거나 가볍게 구는 모습에 써요. 화난 사람이 '지금 장난해요?'라고 하면 놀리지 말라고 따지는 강한 표현이에요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 화나거나 어이없을 때 상대가 가볍게 구는 것을 따지는 말이에요. 친한 사이에서만 쓰세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when you are angry or stunned that the other person is not taking things seriously. Use it only with people you are close to.

explain_en: '장난치다' is the more common word, while '장난하다' fits children playing or someone acting lightly. When an angry person says '지금 장난해요?', it is a sharp way of telling someone to stop fooling around.

examples.en: The school limits phone use.
The doctor limited how much salt I eat.

examples.ko: 이 길은 큰 차의 진입을 제한하고 있어요.
examples.en: This road restricts entry for large vehicles.

examples.ko: 나이를 제한한 행사라서 저는 못 가요.
examples.en: It is an age-restricted event, so I cannot go.
We take the test with a time limit.
From now on I will limit my game time.

explain: 사람이나 규칙이 양, 시간, 대상에 한계를 정할 때 써요. 명사 '제한'은 '시간 제한', '나이 제한'처럼 자주 써요. 스스로 줄이는 것은 '줄이다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when a person or rule sets a ceiling on an amount, a time or who may take part. The noun '제한' is common in '시간 제한' and '나이 제한'. When you cut back by yourself, '줄이다' also works.

examples.en: This is set down by law.

examples.ko: 회사 규칙에 휴가 일수가 규정되어 있어요.
examples.en: The number of vacation days is specified in the company rules.
The school set a separate rule for uniforms.
Please do it as stipulated in the contract.
How are the fines stipulated?
If something is not specified, ask the teacher.

explain: 법, 계약서, 규칙에 적혀 있다는 말이라 보통 문서나 뉴스에서 봐요. 일상 대화에서는 '정해져 있다'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means something is written down in a law, contract or rule, so you mostly see it in documents and the news. In everyday talk, '정해져 있다' is more common.

examples.en: The newspaper criticizes the new policy.
Do not carelessly criticize your friend's opinion.
Many people criticized that movie.
I wrote a piece criticizing the government.

examples.ko: 내용을 읽고 비판할 점을 찾아 봤어요.
examples.en: After reading, I looked for points to criticize.

examples.ko: 기자가 선생님의 방식을 비판해서 논란이 됐어요.
examples.en: A reporter criticized the teacher's method, and it caused controversy.

explain: 이유를 들어 잘못된 점을 따질 때 써요. 그냥 싫다고 하는 '욕하다', '흉보다'와 달라서 뉴스나 글에 자주 나와요. '비난하다'는 더 감정이 실린 말이에요.
explain_en: It means pointing out what is wrong and giving reasons. Unlike '욕하다' or '흉보다', which are just badmouthing, it often appears in news and essays. '비난하다' carries more emotion.

examples.en: The new building will be completed next year.
At last my painting is finished!
When the puzzle is done, I will take a photo.
This dish is only complete once you add the sauce.
It is a song that is not finished yet.
I emailed the completed report.

explain: '끝나다'와 달리 만드는 것이 제대로 갖춰졌다는 느낌이에요. 그림, 건물, 요리처럼 만드는 대상에 써요. 내가 만들어 낼 때는 '완성하다', 만들던 것이 다 갖춰져 끝날 때는 '완성되다'를 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '끝나다', it says that something being made has come together properly. It fits things you make, such as paintings, buildings and dishes. When you make it yourself you say '완성하다', and '완성되다' describes the thing being made reaching its finished state.

examples.en: Our team wins the final.
Korea won yesterday's match.

examples.ko: 끝까지 포기하지 않아서 승리할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: We could win because we did not give up until the end.
The players who won waved their hands.
If we win this time too, we are champions.

examples.ko: 마지막 경기에서 승리하고 나서 모두 울었어요.
examples.en: After winning the last match, everyone cried.

explain: '이기다'가 일상에서 더 흔하고, '승리하다'는 경기나 선거, 전쟁 같은 큰 일에 쓰는 글말 느낌이에요. 반대말은 '패배하다'이고, '지다'가 일상 반대말이에요.
explain_en: '이기다' is more common in daily talk, while '승리하다' has a written feel and suits big events such as matches, elections and wars. Its opposite is '패배하다', and the everyday opposite is '지다'.

examples.ko: 회의 시간이 한 시간 뒤로 조정돼요.
examples.en: The meeting time is adjusted to an hour later.
The price was adjusted last month.
I will tell you right away once the schedule is adjusted.
Please check the adjusted timetable.
The salary was adjusted from this year.
There is a part that has not been adjusted yet.

explain: 일정, 가격, 시간처럼 이미 정해진 것을 상황에 맞게 약간 바꾼다는 말이에요. 완전히 없애는 것이 아니라 맞추는 느낌이라 '취소되다'와 달라요. 안내문에서 자주 봐요.
explain_en: It is used for things already set, such as schedules, prices and times, being changed slightly to fit the situation. It feels like fitting rather than removing, so it differs from '취소되다'. You often see it in notices.

examples.en: I put a chart in my presentation materials.
This song is number one on the music chart.
The hospital checked my chart.

examples.ko: 주식 차트를 보면 값이 오르는 게 보여요.
examples.en: On the stock chart you can see the price going up.

examples.ko: 색깔이 다른 차트가 두 개 있어요.
examples.en: There are two charts in different colors.
Find the highest number on the chart.

explain: 영어 chart에서 온 말이에요. 숫자를 그림으로 보여 주는 표에도, 노래 순위표에도, 병원 기록에도 써요. 사람들은 순위표를 그냥 '차트'라고 부르고 '차트 1위'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It comes from the English word chart. It is used for number graphics, music rankings and hospital records alike. People simply call the ranking list '차트', as in '차트 1위'.

examples.en: Let us suppose it is raining.

examples.ko: 내가 부자라고 가정하면 뭘 할 거예요?
examples.en: If you suppose I am rich, what would you do?
The teacher assumed a problem situation.
I prepare by assuming the worst case.
What is the reason you assumed that?
First I will assume I fail the exam.

explain: 사실인지 모르지만 일단 그렇다고 치고 생각할 때 써요. '만약'이나 '-다면'과 비슷하지만, '가정하다'는 생각의 출발점을 정하는 말이에요. 명사 '가정'은 '가족'이나 '집'의 뜻도 있어서 헷갈리기 쉬워요.
explain_en: You use it when you do not know whether something is true but think as if it were. It is close to '만약' and '-다면', but '가정하다' sets up the starting point of your thinking. The noun '가정' also means a household, so it is easy to confuse.

examples.en: The two people's opinions are identical.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 동일한 색으로 세 벌 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought three of these clothes in the same color.
All students took the test under the same conditions.
Was the price the same?
Please tell me only the parts that are not the same.

examples.ko: 결과가 동일하다면 더 싼 쪽을 고르세요.
examples.en: If the results are the same, choose the cheaper one.

explain: '같다'보다 딱딱해서 문서, 시험, 설명에 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '같아요'라고 하고, 둘이 똑같이 대접받는다는 느낌을 줄 때 '동일하게'를 써요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than '같다' and appears often in documents, exams and explanations. In everyday talk you say '같아요', and '동일하게' gives a sense of being treated equally.

examples.en: He keeps denying the facts.
The company denied the rumor.
You must not deny your own mistake.
No one could deny those words.
I only heard answers that denied it.
You cannot deny this result.

explain: 사실이나 존재를 아니라고 말할 때 써요. '사실을 부정하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 써요. 반대말은 '인정하다'예요. 소리가 같은 '부정(不正)'은 옳지 않은 일이라는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used when you say something is not true or does not exist, with an object as in '사실을 부정하다'. The opposite is '인정하다'. The same-sounding '부정(不正)' is a different word meaning wrongdoing.

examples.en: Cold patients increase in winter.
The number of students has increased a lot this year.

examples.ko: 수입이 증가되면 저금을 더 할 거예요.
examples.en: If my income increases, I will save more.
The company pays the increased cost.
My workload increased, so I am very busy.
There are many regions where the population has not increased.

explain: '늘다'의 글말이라서 숫자나 양이 많아졌다는 보고서와 뉴스에 나와요. 보통은 '증가하다'를 훨씬 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the written-language counterpart of '늘다' and appears in reports and news about numbers or amounts rising. '증가하다' is used much more often.

examples.en: Exercise increases strength.
The company increased production this year.

examples.ko: 홍보를 늘리면 손님을 증가시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you do more promotion, you can bring in more customers.
They say vitamins boost immunity.
I oppose policies that raise taxes.
I increased practice time, and my skills improved.

explain: 사람이나 원인이 직접 양을 늘리는 쪽이에요. 스스로 늘어난 것은 '증가하다', 누가 늘린 것은 '증가시키다'라고 해서 짝이 돼요. 일상에서는 '늘리다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Here a person or cause directly makes an amount grow. It pairs with '증가하다' for things that grow on their own. In everyday speech, '늘리다' sounds more natural.

en: be refused; be rejected; be denied

examples.en: My visa application was rejected.
My proposal gets turned down again.
I was once refused entry at a store.
I could not speak up, fearing I would be rejected.
I keep getting rejected, so I feel upset.
It hurts when a friend rejects you.

explain: '당하다'가 붙어서 내가 받아 주기를 바랐는데 상대가 안 받아 주었다는 속상한 느낌이 있어요. 단순히 안 받아들여진 일은 '거부되다', 상대가 내게 한 일로 느낄 때는 '거부당하다'를 써요.
explain_en: The '당하다' ending adds an unhappy feeling that someone refused you when you wanted it accepted. A plain event of not being accepted uses '거부되다', while '거부당하다' feels like something done to you.

en: be refused; be rejected; be denied

examples.en: The application gets refused.
The payment was declined.
If the password is wrong, access is denied.
It is a request the court rejected.
My card was declined. Why would that be?
To avoid being refused, submit all the documents.

explain: 기계나 제도가 받지 않았다는 사실을 말할 때 자주 써요. 카드 결제, 접속, 신청서에 많이 나와요. 사람에게 거절당한 속상함까지 담으려면 '거부당하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is common for stating that a machine or system did not accept something, such as card payments, logins and applications. To carry the hurt of being turned down by a person, use '거부당하다'.

examples.en: The time is shown on the screen.
The tax is shown on the price tag.

examples.ko: 지도에 우리 집이 빨간 점으로 표시됐어요.
examples.en: Our house was marked with a red dot on the map.
Please wait at the marked spot.
The message is not marked as read.

examples.ko: 이 앱에는 날씨가 숫자로 표시되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I wish this app showed the weather as numbers.

explain: 눈으로 볼 수 있게 화면이나 종이에 나타난다는 말이에요. 앱, 지도, 가격표처럼 정보를 보여 줄 때 자주 나와요. 내가 직접 나타내면 '표시하다', 나타나 있으면 '표시되다'예요.
explain_en: It means information appears on a screen or paper where you can see it, and it is common with apps, maps and price tags. When you do it yourself it is '표시하다', and when it appears it is '표시되다'.

examples.en: How do you interpret this sentence?
The teacher interpreted the poem slowly.
If you read a dream in a good way, you feel good.

examples.ko: 저는 사람들의 꿈을 해석하는 일을 해요.
examples.en: My job is interpreting people's dreams.

examples.ko: 사람마다 해석할 수 있는 방법이 달라요.
examples.en: The way each person can interpret it is different.
I interpreted the results and wrote them in the report.

explain: '번역하다'는 다른 언어로 옮기는 일이고, '해석하다'는 말이나 글, 숫자의 뜻을 풀어서 이해하는 일이에요. 한국어 문장 안에서도 '이 말을 어떻게 해석해요?'처럼 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: '번역하다' means moving text into another language, while '해석하다' means working out the meaning of words, text or numbers. You can use it even within Korean, as in '이 말을 어떻게 해석해요?'.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 새 제품을 위해 협력해요.
examples.en: The two companies cooperate on a new product.
Everyone worked together and finished early.
I want to cooperate with my neighbors.
It is nice to see them cooperating.
I hope we can keep cooperating in the future.
If we do not cooperate, the work gets delayed.

explain: '같이하다'가 단순히 함께하는 것이라면, '협력하다'는 같은 목표를 위해 서로 힘을 보태는 느낌이에요. 회사, 나라, 팀 사이에서 많이 써요. 명사 '협력'은 '협력을 부탁하다'처럼 쓰고요.
explain_en: While '같이하다' just means doing something together, '협력하다' means pooling effort for a shared goal. It is common between companies, countries and teams. The noun '협력' appears in phrases like '협력을 부탁하다'.

examples.en: I build good relationships with friends.

examples.ko: 아이들은 어릴 때 성격을 형성하기 시작해요.
examples.en: Children begin to form their personality when they are young.
The clouds gathered and formed a big rain cloud.
It takes time to form good habits.
A price that has formed does not change right away.
There is a small market that the merchants built up.

explain: 시간이 지나면서 조금씩 모양이 만들어지는 것에 써요. 관계, 습관, 성격, 가격처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에 자주 써요. 물건을 한 번에 만드는 것은 '만들다'를 써요.
explain_en: It describes something taking shape little by little over time. It is often used for things you cannot see, such as relationships, habits, personality and prices. For making a physical object in one go, use '만들다'.

examples.en: The rules get stricter from this year.
Security has been tightened, so entry is hard.
Your muscles get stronger when you exercise.
The strengthened law starts next week.
Once enforcement tightened, accidents decreased.
For the relationship to grow stronger, you need to meet often.

explain: 규칙, 보안, 단속처럼 기준이 더 엄해질 때 자주 써요. 힘이나 관계가 더 단단해질 때도 쓰고요. 반대말은 '약화되다'예요. 뉴스에서 많이 들어요.
explain_en: It is common when standards such as rules, security or enforcement become stricter. It also fits strength or relationships becoming firmer. Its opposite is '약화되다', and you hear it a lot in the news.

examples.en: I will move out of my parents' house next year.
My older brother became independent at twenty.
If you move out on your own, living alone costs money.
I left the company and opened a small shop.
An independent country makes its own laws.
When do you plan to become independent?

explain: 한국에서는 대학을 졸업하거나 취직한 뒤 부모님 집에서 나가 혼자 사는 것을 '독립하다'라고 많이 말해요. 나라가 다른 나라에서 벗어날 때도 쓰고, 직장에서 나와 자기 일을 시작할 때도 써요.
explain_en: In Korea, moving out of your parents' home to live alone, usually after graduating or getting a job, is commonly called '독립하다'. It also describes a country breaking away from another, and leaving a job to start your own work.

examples.en: The accident is reported to the police.
The neighbor's noise was reported to the district office.
Customs checks the declared items.
When a lost item is reported, you get a call.
A problem came up because the marriage was not registered.
My address is registered, so mail comes to me.

explain: 경찰이나 관청에 알려졌다는 말이에요. 사고, 범죄, 이사, 출생처럼 알려야 하는 일에 써요. 내가 알리면 '신고하다', 알려지면 '신고되다'예요.
explain_en: It means something has been reported to the police or a government office, such as an accident, a crime, a move or a birth. When you report it you say '신고하다', and when it gets reported it is '신고되다'.

examples.en: The teacher does not discriminate among students.
You must not discriminate against people because of age.
That shop treats customers unequally.
There was a time they treated someone differently for being foreign.
It hurts to hear discriminating words.

examples.ko: 누구도 차별할 수 없다고 법에 쓰여 있어요.
examples.en: The law says no one may be discriminated against.

explain: 사람을 이유 없이 다르게 대할 때 써요. 단순히 '구별하다'와 달리 불공평하다는 나쁜 뜻이 있어요. 당하는 쪽은 '차별을 받다'나 '차별당하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes treating people differently for no good reason. Unlike plain '구별하다', it carries a negative sense of unfairness. The person on the receiving end says '차별을 받다' or '차별당하다'.

examples.en: It is open only on certain days.

examples.ko: 이 약은 특정한 병에만 효과가 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine works only for a specific illness.

examples.ko: 특정하게 정해진 사람만 이 방에 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only specifically designated people can enter this room.
I do not use only one particular company's products.
It is a letter sent to no particular person.
The police pinned down the culprit and caught him right away.

explain: '특정'은 '어떤 정해진'이라는 느낌으로 명사 앞에 많이 붙어요. 보통 '특정한 사람', '특정 회사'처럼 말해요. 동사 '특정하다'는 범인을 특정하다처럼 수사 뉴스에서도 들려요.
explain_en: '특정' mostly attaches to a noun to mean a fixed, particular one, as in '특정한 사람' or '특정 회사'. The verb '특정하다' also appears in crime news, for example pinning down a suspect.

examples.en: Your member information gets registered.
My name was registered at the school.
A text goes to the registered number.
Once the car is registered, a license plate is issued.
My address has not been registered yet.
I am glad the photo got registered in the app.

explain: 이름, 번호, 차, 회원처럼 공식 명단에 올라갔다는 말이에요. 내가 하면 '등록하다', 올라가 있으면 '등록되다'예요. 학원에 이름을 올릴 때는 '등록하다'를 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means a name, number, car or member has been put on an official list. When you do it, it is '등록하다', and when it ends up on the list it is '등록되다'. For signing up at an academy, '등록하다' is common.

examples.en: This bread is made from wheat.
The wheat in the field has ripened yellow.
I have a wheat allergy.
Korea imports most of its wheat.

examples.ko: 쌀 대신 밀을 먹는 나라도 많아요.
examples.en: Many countries eat wheat instead of rice.
The price of wheat went up this year.

explain: 밀을 갈면 '밀가루'가 돼요. '밀'은 '밀다'의 어간과 소리가 같지만 다른 말이라서 문장에서 구별해요. 빵, 국수, 수제비의 재료예요.
explain_en: When wheat is ground it becomes '밀가루', flour. The noun '밀' sounds the same as the stem of the verb '밀다' (to push), but they are different words, so tell them apart in the sentence. It is the ingredient in bread, noodles and sujebi.

en: make someone perceive; make someone aware of

examples.en: Ads make people aware of a new product.
I made students realize how serious the problem is.
I put up a poster to raise awareness of safety.
After making him realize his mistake, I received an apology.
You need to make the child aware of the rules.
If you repeat it to make them aware, people remember.

explain: 상대가 어떤 사실을 분명히 알게 만들 때 써요. 스스로 알게 되는 것은 '인식하다', 남이 알게 하는 것은 '인식시키다'예요. 말하기에서는 '알려 주다'나 '깨닫게 하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is used when you make someone clearly aware of a fact. Becoming aware by yourself is '인식하다', and making others aware is '인식시키다'. In speech, '알려 주다' or '깨닫게 하다' sounds more natural.

en: be achieved; be accomplished; be attained

examples.en: The goal is achieved.
This year's sales target was achieved.
Everyone worked hard, and the plan was accomplished.
Please write the achieved numbers in the table.
At this pace it is hard for the goal to be reached.
There are many things not achieved yet.

explain: '이루다'는 소원과 꿈에도 쓰지만, '달성되다'는 매출, 점수, 목표처럼 숫자로 잴 수 있는 것에 많이 써요. 내가 해내면 '달성하다', 결과로 이루어지면 '달성되다'예요.
explain_en: '이루다' also fits wishes and dreams, but '달성되다' is mostly used for things you can measure, such as sales, scores and targets. When you accomplish it yourself it is '달성하다', and when it comes about as a result it is '달성되다'.

examples.en: I complete all my homework.
I finished filling out the application.
When the installation completes, the app opens.
They will finish the construction by today.
A text arrives after you complete the payment.
We finished all preparations and set off.

explain: '끝내다'보다 딱딱하고, 정해진 일이 끝났을 때 써요. 앱 화면에 '완료'라고 뜨는 것도 같은 말이에요. 말할 때는 '다 했어요', '마쳤어요'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than '끝내다' and is used when a set task is done. The word '완료' shown on app screens is the same word. In speech, '다 했어요' or '마쳤어요' is more common.

examples.en: The spacecraft launch is tomorrow.
I watched the rocket launch on TV.
The launch was postponed because of the weather.
A loud sound came at the moment of launch.
The news said the satellite launch succeeded.
There are ten minutes left until launch.

explain: 주로 로켓, 우주선, 인공위성처럼 하늘로 보내는 일에 써요. '발사 성공', '발사 시간'처럼 명사끼리 이어 말하는 일이 많아요. '발사하다', '발사되다'와 같은 뿌리의 말이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for sending rockets, spacecraft and satellites into the sky. Nouns often chain with it, as in '발사 성공' and '발사 시간'. It shares a root with '발사하다' and '발사되다'.

en: be fired; be launched; be set off

examples.en: The rocket is launched today.
The satellite was launched yesterday.
Fireworks were shot into the sky.

examples.ko: 발사된 우주선이 지구 둘레를 돌고 있어요.
examples.en: The launched spacecraft is orbiting the Earth.
A launch can happen only when the weather is good.
It is a rocket that has not been launched yet.

explain: 로켓, 우주선, 불꽃놀이 같은 것이 공중으로 쏘아 올려지는 것이 주어예요. 쏘는 사람이 주어면 '발사하다', 쏘아지는 것이 주어면 '발사되다'를 써요.
explain_en: The subject is the thing being shot up into the air, such as a rocket, a spacecraft or fireworks. If the subject is the one firing it, use '발사하다'. If the subject is the thing being fired, use '발사되다'.

examples.en: Scientists launch a rocket.
The company launched a satellite.
They set off fireworks at the end of the festival.
The plan is to launch the spacecraft tomorrow.
The place where they launched the rocket is by the sea.
They run a check before launching.

explain: 쏘아 올리는 사람이나 기관이 주어예요. '쏘다'와 달리 로켓, 위성, 불꽃처럼 큰 것을 올릴 때 많이 써요. 활이나 총에는 '쏘다'를 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: The subject is the person or organization doing the launching. Unlike plain '쏘다', it is used often for big equipment like rockets, satellites and fireworks. For arrows and guns, people say '쏘다' more often.

en: be written; be filled in; be drawn up

examples.en: Documents are drawn up on a computer.
The contract was drawn up yesterday.
This text was written in Korean.
Please check the written report.
Once the application is filled in, I will accept it.
There is a box that has not been filled in yet.

explain: 서류, 보고서, 계약서처럼 공식적으로 써서 만드는 글에 써요. 일기나 편지처럼 가볍게 쓴 글은 '쓰여 있다'가 더 자연스러워요. 내가 쓰면 '작성하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used for texts written up in an official way, such as documents, reports and contracts. For lighter writing like diaries and letters, '쓰여 있다' sounds more natural. When you write it yourself, use '작성하다'.

examples.en: A picture is presented in the exam.
A new opinion was put forward at the meeting.
The price is shown on the website.
Answer according to the conditions given.

examples.ko: 좋은 방법이 제시되면 따라 해 볼게요.
examples.en: If a good method is put forward, I will try it.
The correct answer was not given in the question.

explain: 시험, 회의, 안내문에서 어떤 내용이 눈앞에 내밀어질 때 써요. 내가 보여 주면 '제시하다'예요. 신분증이나 표를 보여 달라고 할 때는 '제시해 주세요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used in exams, meetings and notices when some content is put in front of you. When you present it, use '제시하다'. When asked to show an ID or ticket, the phrase is '제시해 주세요'.

examples.en: The train passes through the tunnel.
I passed the document screening.

examples.ko: 검사대를 통과하면 비행기를 탈 수 있어요.
examples.en: After going through the checkpoint, you can board the plane.
This bill will pass the National Assembly.

examples.ko: 시험을 통과한 사람은 다음 주에 와요.
examples.en: People who passed the test come next week.
It was hard to get through the narrow door.

explain: 장소를 지나갈 때도, 시험이나 심사를 넘길 때도 써요. 시험에서 점수를 받아 붙는 것은 '합격하다'를 더 자주 말하고, 서류나 심사에는 '통과하다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It works both for passing through a place and for getting past an exam or screening. For passing an exam by score, '합격하다' is more common, while '통과하다' suits document reviews and screenings.

examples.en: I will establish a company next year.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 백 년 전에 한 선교사가 설립했어요.
examples.en: A missionary founded this school a hundred years ago.

examples.ko: 친구와 같이 작은 출판사를 설립하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to found a small publishing company with a friend.
The person who set up the foundation was a teacher.
There is a plan to establish a new library.
You need documents to establish an organization.

explain: 회사, 학교, 단체처럼 공식적인 조직을 새로 세울 때 써요. 집이나 건물은 '짓다'를 쓰고, 가게를 여는 것은 '차리다'나 '열다'를 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when you newly set up an official organization such as a company, school or group. For houses and buildings use '짓다', and for opening a shop '차리다' or '열다' is more common.

examples.en: That friend's words are sincere.
I felt better after receiving a sincere apology.
His eyes looked sincere.

examples.ko: 진실하게 말하면 모두가 이해해 줄 거예요.
examples.en: If you speak honestly, everyone will understand.
You quickly notice compliments that are not sincere.

examples.ko: 진실하고 따뜻한 친구는 힘들 때 곁에 있어요.
examples.en: A sincere and warm friend stays by your side in hard times.

explain: '솔직하다'는 숨기지 않고 말한다는 느낌이고, '진실하다'는 마음과 말에 거짓이 없다는 느낌이에요. 사람의 성격에 써요. 사실을 말하는 명사 '진실'과 같은 뿌리의 말이에요.
explain_en: '솔직하다' feels like speaking without hiding anything, while '진실하다' feels like having no falseness in heart and words. It describes a person's character. It shares a root with the noun '진실', meaning the truth.

examples.ko: 결과를 보면 이 방법이 더 좋다고 판단돼요.
examples.en: Judging by the results, this method seems better.
It was judged unsafe, so we cancelled.
If it is judged dangerous, tell me right away.
Only people judged to have no problem go in.
It has not been judged exactly yet.
Please explain why it was judged that way.

explain: '-라고 판단되다' 모양으로 많이 나오고, 자료를 보고 결론을 낸다는 글말 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '그런 것 같아요'를 더 자주 말해요. 내가 판단하면 '판단하다'예요.
explain_en: It most often appears as '-라고 판단되다', and it has a written feel of reaching a conclusion from the evidence. In everyday talk, '그런 것 같아요' is more common. When you judge it yourself, use '판단하다'.

examples.en: My father runs a small restaurant.
I want to run a company myself.

examples.ko: 호텔을 경영한 지 십 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been ten years since I started running the hotel.
They say running a business is not easy.
I learned a lot while running the store.
How will you run the school from now on?

explain: 회사나 가게의 돈, 사람, 일을 책임지고 이끌 때 써요. 작은 가게는 '운영하다'를 더 자주 쓰고, '경영하다'는 회사나 사업 같은 큰 곳에 어울려요.
explain_en: It means taking charge of the money, people and work of a company or shop. '운영하다' is used more for small shops, while '경영하다' fits companies and businesses.

examples.ko: 조건이 모두 만족되면 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can apply once all conditions are met.

examples.ko: 수요가 만족되자 줄을 서는 사람이 줄었어요.
examples.en: Once the demand was met, fewer people stood in line.
The demand was not satisfied, so I complained.

examples.ko: 이 식이 만족되는 숫자를 찾아 보세요.
examples.en: Find the number that satisfies this equation.
All standards were satisfied.

examples.ko: 필요가 만족된 뒤에는 더 사지 않아요.
examples.en: After the need is met, I do not buy more.

explain: 기분이 좋다는 '만족하다'와 달리, 조건이나 요구가 채워졌다는 쪽에 자주 써요. 수학과 서류에서도 나와요. 사람이 느끼는 만족은 '만족하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike '만족하다', which is about feeling pleased, '만족되다' is often about conditions or demands being fulfilled. It also appears in math and paperwork. A person's feeling of satisfaction is '만족하다'.

examples.en: Good service satisfies customers.
It is hard to satisfy everyone.
The delicious food satisfied the guests.
I want to get grades that will please my parents.
We are looking for someone who meets the conditions.
I satisfied the teacher and got praised.

explain: 내가 상대를 만족하게 만든다는 말이에요. 내가 만족하는 것은 '만족하다', 남을 만족하게 하는 것은 '만족시키다'로 갈라요. 일상 대화에서는 '마음에 들게 하다'를 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It means making the other person feel satisfied. Feeling satisfied yourself is '만족하다', and making others satisfied is '만족시키다'. In daily talk, people sometimes say '마음에 들게 하다'.

examples.en: The heat continued for a month.
Good things happened one after another.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 세 번 연속하여 이겼어요.
examples.en: Our team won three times in a row.
If all-night work continues, your body gets tired.
Write down consecutive numbers.
How many years in a row did the record continue?

explain: '계속하다'는 하던 일을 이어서 한다는 뜻이고, '연속하다'는 같은 일이 끊기지 않고 이어진다는 느낌이에요. '연속해서', '세 번 연속'처럼 부사 모양으로도 써요.
explain_en: '계속하다' means carrying on with something you were doing, while '연속하다' feels like the same thing following without a break. It also appears in adverb forms such as '연속해서' and '세 번 연속'.

examples.en: The two countries become one.
The uniforms in our class are now uniform.
Once the opinions are unified, we start right away.

examples.ko: 글꼴이 통일된 발표 자료가 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: Presentation materials with a uniform font look good.
The method has not been unified yet.
I hope the method will be unified by next week.

explain: 한국에서는 남한과 북한의 '통일'이 큰 주제라서 뉴스에 자주 나와요. 표, 글꼴, 의견처럼 서로 달랐던 것이 하나로 맞춰질 때도 써요.
explain_en: In Korea, the unification of South and North Korea is a big topic, so the word appears often in the news. It is also used when different tables, fonts or opinions are brought into line.

examples.en: The volcano suddenly erupts.
Gas exploded at the factory.
The anger I held back finally burst out.
Everyone evacuated before the bomb exploded.
Its popularity is exploding right now.
Be careful, because it could explode.

explain: 물건이 터질 때뿐 아니라 감정이 한꺼번에 터질 때도 써요. 인기나 관심이 갑자기 커질 때 '폭발적이다'라고도 해요. 작은 풍선은 '터지다'를 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It describes things blowing up, and also emotions bursting out all at once. When popularity or interest suddenly grows, people say '폭발적이다'. For a small balloon, '터지다' is more common.

examples.en: The government reforms the education system.
They picked a new head to reform the company.
We reformed the old way, and work got faster.
After the reform, the students liked it.
I want to reform this rule.
We have to decide what to reform first.

explain: 제도, 조직, 규칙 같은 큰 것을 근본부터 바꾼다는 말이에요. 작은 물건이나 습관은 '고치다', '바꾸다'를 써요. 뉴스에서는 '개혁'이라는 명사 모양으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means changing something big, such as a system, organization or rule, from its foundations. For small objects or habits use '고치다' or '바꾸다'. In the news it often appears as the noun '개혁'.
